spec: folder format spec section 4.7, the archive (drafted 2026-10-22), on 0.3.12; tests OW-1..OW-22
notes: reader: what a reader does with the file (accept, or refuse with `reason`). Every reader runner checks this field.

writer: whether the file is one a conforming writer may emit as a portable .owworld, checked against `source` (every source file present byte-exact) and the writer's MUST rules (only the folder's parts, a marker only in its shape, no api, 1980 stamps, UTF-8 byte order, methods 0 and 8). A SHOULD never makes it refuse; `should` names one a fixture breaks. Only a reference checker checks it; the role says which side the test is about.
role: reader | writer | roundtrip. A writer fixture is still opened by every reader: its `reader` verdict says so.
strips: a key a reader removes from world.json and never returns (OW-10: `api`), the file still read.
open: what section 4.7 still leaves open on this fixture (the question, with the spec's line); the verdict follows `lean` and moves when the spec says otherwise. Every other verdict is the spec's.
reason: one of `reasons` (section 4.7: the TypeScript reader's six plus duplicate, collision, link, method, name, marker). A reader that refuses for another cause fails the case.

budget: reader verdicts hold for a reader whose budget is the floor (`floor`: 500,000 entries, 2 GiB). A reader whose budget is larger reads the fixtures marked `budget: floor` with the floor's budget; one whose budget is smaller fails the floor cases (pass-OW-15-floor, pass-OW-15-floor-bytes).

source: a fixture's writer verdict is checked against `source` unless it names one of `sources` (the private case's world, OW-8). A source's `private` lists producers marked private in its RECORDS.json (section 4.5 rule 11): each one's directory is present whole and byte-exact, or absent whole; the manifest itself travels byte-exact either way.

side: on the private case, which side of the export the file is: `default` (private records left out) or `asked` (the caller asked for them). Both are files a conforming writer emits; which one depends on the call, not the bytes.

fixtures.rule: The good world: one top folder, a string id, records/ whole (its own world.json, dot-file and x.meta included), sorted, 1980 stamps, methods 0 and 8.
The content decides, not the name: pass-good's exact bytes under .zip read the same.
A JSON export renamed .owworld is not a zip: refused.
world.json at the archive's root is the same world (spec section 4: readers also accept it).
Two top folders each holding world.json: two worlds, refused.
world.json at the root and in a top folder: two worlds, refused.
world.json only two folders down (x/y/world.json): no world, refused.
No world.json anywhere a world may sit: refused.
world.json has no id: not a world, refused.
world.json has a numeric id (7): not a world, refused.
world.json has a blank id: not a world, refused.
world.json is a JSON array, not an object: not a world, refused.
world.json does not parse: not a world, refused.
A README.txt beside the world's folder: a reader ignores it; a writer never emits it.

A tool's dot-folder beside the world, holding its own world.json (Unity's UT fixture shape, which section 4.7 names: accept): a dot-folder is never a world; a reader ignores it, a writer never emits it.
Archive junk a re-zip picks up (__MACOSX/, .DS_Store): never part of a world; ignored by a reader.
A world.json inside the world (abbey/inner/world.json), not under records/: refused. (pass-good holds records/lab/world.json, which must pass.)
mimetype first, stored, no extra field, exactly application/vnd.onlyworlds.world+zip: accepted (and pass-good, with none, is accepted too: a reader MUST NOT require it).
A mimetype entry holding application/zip: a marker present with other bytes, refused.
The right string with a trailing newline: the bytes are exactly the media type, ASCII, no newline; other bytes, refused.

The UTF-8 byte order mark before the media type: a reader that decodes the entry as text first drops the mark and passes it (the TypeScript reader did until SDK 4.53.2); the bytes are compared as bytes, so these are other bytes, refused.
The right bytes, deflated: a reader reads it (its bytes are the media type); a writer stores the marker, so it reads from the file's opening bytes.
The right bytes, stored, but sorted after abbey/...: a reader reads it; a writer puts the marker first.
Writer: a README.md in the world's folder is not one of the folder's parts (world.json, elements/, spatial/, media/, records/); a reader still opens the file.
Writer: a .git/ folder is not one of the folder's parts (world.json, elements/, spatial/, media/, records/); a reader still opens the file.
Writer: Unity's .meta beside an element is not one of the folder's parts (world.json, elements/, spatial/, media/, records/); a reader still opens the file.

Writer: a tool's .atlas/ folder (a private copy when the caller asks, never a portable .owworld) is not one of the folder's parts (world.json, elements/, spatial/, media/, records/); a reader still opens the file.
Writer: records/lab/ledger.bin left out; records/ travels whole (section 4.5 rule 6a).
Writer: ledger.bin re-encoded (CRLF to LF, BOM stripped); records/ travels byte-exact.
Writer: the producer's own ledger.bin.meta dropped as if it were Unity's litter.
Writer, the default side: records/fold/ is marked private in RECORDS.json, so an export, share or snapshot leaves the whole directory out; RECORDS.json travels byte-exact, its fold entry kept.
Writer, the asked side: the caller asked for private records, so records/fold/ travels whole and byte-exact, its dot-file included, like any producer's.
Writer: records/fold/ half carried (.head in, spine.jsonl out); a private directory goes whole or not at all.
Writer: records/fold/ left out and its entry cut from RECORDS.json; the manifest travels byte-exact, so a reader learns a private producer was left out rather than never there.
Read then write: entries a reader does not understand inside the folder's parts (an element type that is not one of the 22, a media file of no known kind) come back byte-equal, records/ included.

A private copy (a tool's .atlas/ carried): not a portable .owworld (OW-7), so a writer making one never emits it; a reader that rewrites it passes .atlas/charts.json and records/ through byte-equal (OW-9).
world.json carries an api block with a key: a reader strips it, never returns it, and reads the world; a writer never emits it.
Writer: world.json lost source and exported_as (section 4.1: a copy drops nothing but api).
Writer: world.json gained snapshot_at, which the source lacked (a portable copy invents nothing).
Writer: entries stamped with a clock (2026-10-21 12:00), not 1980-01-01.
Writer: entries in reverse order; a writer sorts them.
Writer: sorted by the UTF-8 bytes of the name: media/Ａ.png (U+FF21) before media/😀.png (U+1F600).
Writer: sorted by UTF-16 code units (C# ordinal, JS <), which puts U+1F600 before U+FF21.

An entry that truly inflates to 2.25 GiB of zeros (sizes honest, about 2.3 MB on disk): past the 2 GiB floor, so a reader holding the floor's budget refuses it from its declared size, before inflating.
An element declares 64 bytes and inflates to 4090 (its CRC is the true one): a size that lies is refused when it is inflated.
A stored entry declares 64 bytes and holds 73: the same lie as a deflated one, the same cause.
A stored entry declares 137 bytes and holds 73: fewer than it declares is a broken entry, not_openable (only more is too_big; ruled 2026-10-22).
An element whose bytes fail the CRC its headers declare (one bit off; folder spec 4.7's size bullet): refused, never read as written.

An element's deflate stream ends 4 bytes before the compressed size its headers declare, those bytes junk (FF FF FF FF); its inflated size and CRC are honest. The entry holds fewer deflate bytes than it declares, so its declared size lies: a broken entry, not_openable, never read by stopping at the stream's end and ignoring the rest.

An element's deflate stream never ends: every byte a literal, no end-of-block code, its sizes and CRC honest. A reader refuses an archive whose stream it cannot read to its declared end (folder spec 4.7's size bullet, ruled 2026-10-24), never one that stops once it holds the declared bytes.
The good world with a zip64 end of central directory (record and locator, the classic record's counts 0xFFFF): the structure a world past 65,535 entries needs, read on ten files.
fixtures.should: A writer SHOULD write a classic zip under 65,535 entries: this structure on ten files is one every reader reads, not one a writer makes.

fixtures.rule: The entry ../x.json climbs out or is absolute: refused.
The entry abbey/../x.json climbs out or is absolute: refused.
The entry /etc/x.json climbs out or is absolute: refused.
The entry C:/x.json climbs out or is absolute: refused.
The entry \\server\x.json climbs out or is absolute: refused.
The entry abbey\elements\character\cora--0000ab04.json is not a plain relative path: refused, whatever it would resolve to.
The entry abbey//elements/character/cora--0000ab04.json is not a plain relative path: refused, whatever it would resolve to.
The entry abbey/./elements/character/cora--0000ab04.json is not a plain relative path: refused, whatever it would resolve to.
The entry abbey/elements/../elements/character/cora--0000ab04.json is not a plain relative path: refused, whatever it would resolve to.
abbey/elements/character/ana--0000ab01.json twice, different bodies: refused.
README.txt twice beside the world: a duplicate anywhere in the archive is refused.
Cora.json and cora.json: one file on Windows and macOS, refused.
media/café.png in NFC (U+00E9) and NFD (e + U+0301), both flagged UTF-8: one name, refused.
abbey/Elements/ beside abbey/elements/: one folder on a case-insensitive disk, refused.
media/Café.png (NFD, capital C) and media/café.png (NFC): neither NFC alone nor case folding alone joins them; NFC then folding does. Refused.
media/σ.png (U+03C3) and media/ς.png (U+03C2, final sigma): simple case folding maps U+03C2 to U+03C3 (lowercasing does not); one name, refused.

media/ﬅ.png (U+FB05, long s t) and media/ﬆ.png (U+FB06, s t): NFC keeps them apart; the S row of CaseFolding.txt 15.1.0 maps U+FB05 to U+FB06, the pair a runtime's lowercase misses. One name, refused.
media/ΐ.png (U+1FD3) and media/ΐ.png (U+0390): NFC already makes them one (U+1FD3 is a canonical singleton), before the S row that says the same; one name, refused.
media/straße.png and media/strasse.png: simple case folding leaves U+00DF alone (full folding makes it 'ss'); two names, accepted.

media/豈.png (U+F900, a CJK compatibility ideograph) and media/豈.png (U+8C48): U+F900's decomposition is the one code point U+8C48 (a singleton), and no case folding applies, so only NFC joins them. One name, refused.

media/Å.png (U+212B ANGSTROM SIGN) and media/Å.png (A + U+030A): NFC takes U+212B to U+00C5 (a singleton, never recomposed) and composes A + U+030A to U+00C5. Against U+00C5 itself the pair needs no NFC (CaseFolding's C rows take U+212B and U+00C5 both to U+00E5), so the other side is the decomposed one: folding alone leaves a + U+030A. One name, refused.

media/क़.png (U+0958 DEVANAGARI LETTER QA) and media/क़.png (U+0915 U+093C): U+0958 decomposes to U+0915 U+093C and is a composition exclusion, so NFC of both is U+0915 U+093C, never U+0958. One name, refused. (A reader that wrongly recomposes U+0958 joins them too: no case folding applies to an excluded character, so no pair of names can show that fault; NormalizationTest does.)

media/lệ.png and media/lệ.png (e + dot below U+0323, class 220, and circumflex U+0302, class 230, in either order): canonical ordering puts U+0323 first, and both compose to U+1EC7. A reader that composes without ordering gets U+1EC7 and U+00EA U+0323, two names. One name, refused.

media/lá̀.png and media/là́.png (acute U+0301 and grave U+0300, both class 230, in either order): marks of one class keep their order, so NFC gives U+00E1 U+0300 and U+00E0 U+0301. A reader that sorts marks by code point, or unstably, joins them. Two names, accepted.

media/한.png (U+D55C, the syllable han) and media/한.png (its jamo U+1112 U+1161 U+11AB): Hangul composes by arithmetic (L+V, then LV+T), not by UnicodeData's field 5, which lists no syllable. One name, refused.

media/ΐ.png (iota + U+0344, a mark whose decomposition U+0308 U+0301 starts with a non-starter: excluded from composition) and media/ΐ.png: NFC decomposes U+0344 and composes both to U+0390. One name, refused.

media/ﬁ.png (U+FB01, the fi ligature) and media/fi.png: U+FB01's mapping is <compat>, so NFC keeps it (NFKC would not), and CaseFolding has only an F row for it (simple folding keeps it; a runtime's full casefold would not). Two names, accepted.

media/𑎃.png (U+11383) and media/𑎃.png (U+11382 U+113C9): Tulu-Tigalari, new in Unicode 16.0, where U+11383 decomposes to U+11382 U+113C9 and NFC joins them. At the pinned 15.1.0 all three are unassigned, so each is its own NFC: two names, accepted. A reader whose NFC is its runtime's at 16.0 (Python 3.14's unicodedata, Node 22's ICU 76) joins them and refuses with collision.
abbey/media is a file and abbey/media/a.png sits under it: refused.
An entry whose Unix mode is a symlink (0o120777), target ../../etc/passwd: refused.
Regular files (0o100644, Unix-made) and a directory entry (0o040755): accepted.
An element entry in LZMA (method 14): only stored and deflate, never encrypted; refused, not skipped.
An element entry in deflate64 (method 9; its data stored blocks, valid deflate64): only stored and deflate, never encrypted; refused, not skipped.
An element entry in ZipCrypto (general-purpose bit 0; password 'owworld'): only stored and deflate, never encrypted; refused, not skipped.
The good world's bytes, its end record saying this is disk 1 of a spanned set whose directory starts on disk 0: nothing spanned, refused.
The entry 'abbey/elements/character/CON.json' has a Windows reserved name (CON): refused.
The entry 'abbey/media/nul.txt' has a Windows reserved name with an extension (nul.txt): refused.
The entry 'abbey/media/lpt1.png' has a numbered Windows reserved name (lpt1.png): refused.
The entry 'abbey/media/a.png.' has a trailing dot: refused.
The entry 'abbey/media/b.png ' has a trailing space: refused.
The entry 'abbey/media/a?.png' has a reserved character (?): refused.
The entry 'abbey/media/a\x01.png' has a control character (U+0001): refused.
A non-ASCII name (UTF-8 bytes) without the UTF-8 flag (bit 11): its decoding is a guess, refused.
A name with the UTF-8 flag whose bytes are not UTF-8 (a Latin-1 e acute, 0xE9): its spelling is a guess, refused.
con--0000e1.json: its base name is con--0000e1, not a reserved name; accepted.
One entry past the floor (500,001 files), read with the floor's budget: refused.
fixtures.why: 500,001 entries (zip64) come to about 112 MB. Made on demand by `generate.py --large DIR`, never part of the set.

fixtures.rule: A world of exactly 500,000 entries (zip64), the floor: every reader accepts it.
fixtures.why: About 112 MB. Made on demand by `generate.py --large DIR`. pass-OW-15-zip64 carries the zip64 structure in the set.

fixtures.rule: A world whose files inflate to just under 2 GiB in all (one entry of zeros, sizes honest): every reader accepts it.
fixtures.why: About 2 MB on disk, but reading it inflates 2 GiB: never run by default. Made on demand by `generate.py --large DIR`.
